`final class VulkanFrameAllocator`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.backend.vulkan.render.buffer` · **Module:** `backend-vulkan` · **Source:** [VulkanFrameAllocator.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/backend/vulkan/src/main/java/dev/joid/backend/vulkan/render/buffer/VulkanFrameAllocator.java)<br/>
**Backends:** <span class="joid-badge">Vulkan</span>

Hands out aligned ranges of one buffer for the vertices or the uniforms of a frame, reset when the slot of the frame comes back.

- [What it is made of](/build/backends/vulkan/#what-it-is-made-of)

## Creation details

<a id="VulkanFrameAllocator-constructor"></a>

### VulkanFrameAllocator

`VulkanFrameAllocator(VulkanContext context, long capacity, int usage, long alignment, Consumer<Runnable> disposer)` 

Creates the allocator with a buffer of that capacity in bytes, that usage and that alignment; the consumer defers the destruction of a buffer that grew.

## Method details

<a id="VulkanFrameAllocator-method-destroy"></a>

### destroy

`void destroy()` 

Destroys the current buffer.

<a id="VulkanFrameAllocator-method-allocate"></a>

### allocate

`long allocate(long size)` 

Returns the offset of an aligned range of that size in the current buffer.
When the buffer is full, it replaces it with a buffer twice as large, defers the destruction of the old one, and returns `0`.

<a id="VulkanFrameAllocator-method-reset"></a>

### reset

`void reset()` 

Makes the whole buffer free again, at the start of a frame of its slot.

<a id="VulkanFrameAllocator-method-getUsage"></a>

### getUsage

`int getUsage()` 

Returns the usage of the buffers.

<a id="VulkanFrameAllocator-method-getAlignment"></a>
